Hi Team,
In Sollich 1, with the new Hopper level configuration, when the Hopper reaches the high level, the drain valve opens to the caramel barrel to release pressure from the piping.

If this happens frequently during a shift, the barrel could fill multiple times, potentially resulting in two barrels of caramel scrap.

To avoid this, I was looking for a balance point where the caramel flow from the pump at 44.8 Hz matches the amount of caramel being injected onto the belt at a belt speed of 72 1/min.

However, when the belt stops for a metal detector test, 44.2 Hz is not enough flow to restart the system properly. Therefore, I configured the low level at 85% and the high level at 90%.

With this configuration, the system operates throughout the day without requiring any additional adjustments or manipulation.
